newsitem.title: UK: UK regulator urges Railtrack freight action.
newsitem.headline: UK regulator urges Railtrack freight action.

text.p: Britain's railway industry regulator on Wednesday called on rail infrastructure operator Railtrack Group Plc to stick by plans to improve the freight industry.

"The Railtrack 10-point plan for the development of freight is a step in the right direction. Turning the words into deeds is the test and the regulator has asked Railtrack to report progress to him by the end of July," Martin Brennan, freight director for the Office of the Rail Regulator said in a statement.
Railtrack, which on Thursday will announce its first results since privatisation, pledged in April to invest a further 20 million stg to develop 30 freight terminals.

The proposal followed a 15-billion stg spending plan unveiled in February which Railtrack said aimed to create one of the world's most efficient rail networks and siphon freight from the roads to the railway.
Railtrack, criticised by regulators for sluggish investment, is expected to face more calls from regulators and the newly-elected Labour government to improve the railway system.
The company could also be hit by a threatened windfall tax on the profits of privatised companies.
